title: Remembering Zhu Rongji
gist: Obituary of former premier Zhu Rongji (died at 97 in August) crediting him with China's growth surge and WTO entry, but tracing today's crisis to his early-1990s tax-recentralisation bargain that let provinces run their own banks, fuelling a local-government land and property boom whose 2021 crash wiped out an estimated $18tn of household wealth and now drives export overcapacity ('China shock 2.0').

insights.claim: Per Minxin Pei, Zhu's economic policies drove an eightfold increase in China's economy and a 600% rise in per-capita income between 1978 and 2002.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Context for China's reform-era growth model now exhausted.

insights.claim: Zhu's early-1990s recentralisation of tax revenue was bought by letting provinces set up their own banks and raise and spend money without close central supervision, a bargain China still struggles with.

insights.so_what: Root cause of China's local-government debt problem.
insights.quote: China is still struggling with the long-term consequences of that bargain.
